properties.context: CEO Hock Tan serves on Meta board while Meta is potential customer/counterparty
Director Harry You serves on IonQ board while director compensation and potential business relationships create circular dependency

director_comp.notes: [chunk 1/1] FILING CONTEXT: AVGO (Broadcom) DEF 14A filed 2024-02-26. SECTION: Director Compensation and Director Nominees. SIFI-MATERIAL FINDINGS: (1) CEO RELATED-PARTY CONCENTRATION: Hock E. Tan (President & CEO since 2006) does not receive compensation from Broadcom board service but sits on Meta Platforms board. This creates a circularity: Broadcom supplies networking/semiconductor components to Meta data centers; Tan's board seat at Meta gives him inside knowledge of Meta's capex/demand signals, creating potential conflicts-of-interest and information asymmetries. (2) DIRECTOR EXTERNAL BOARD SEAT CONCENTRATION: Harry L. You (director, Audit & Compensation Chair) serves on IonQ board. IonQ is an AI quantum computing company that may be a customer or technology partner to Broadcom's AI infrastructure business. This creates circularity in compensation oversight (You chairs Compensation Committee while having external equity interests). (3) KENNETH HAO / SILVER LAKE CIRCULARITY: Hao joined Broadcom board in Feb 2024 as Chairman/Managing Partner of Silver Lake (global tech investment firm). Silver Lake likely has significant invested capital in Broadcom suppliers, customers, or competitors (SolarWinds, Splunk portfolio companies). Hao also sits on SolarWinds and Splunk boards — both security/infrastructure software companies competing with or complementing Broadcom's security offerings. This multi-seat arrangement creates information cascades and potential conflicts. (4) JUSTINE PAGE INSIDER HISTORY: Page is Chair of Audit Committee. She was previously a director of Broadcom Limited (2016-2017) and Avago Technologies Limited (2008-2016). She chairs the Audit Committee of a company she previously served on, which may create familiarity bias in oversight. Not egregious but worth noting. EXTRACTED ENTITIES: (a) Broadcom (AVGO) — filer, supplier role. (b) Meta — customer/strategic counterparty via CEO Tan board seat. (c) Silver Lake — investor/influence node via Kenneth Hao. (d) IonQ — potential customer/technology partner, director circularity via You. (e) SolarWinds, Splunk — portfolio/competitor nodes for Hao. SKIP: Haemonetics (Bryant), Flowserve (Delly), Littelfuse (Delly), SIRIUS XM (Hartenstein), Singapore Telecom (Low), GTY Technology (You), Coupang (You), dMY SPACs (You) — these are generic director seat listings not SIFI-material to Broadcom's core counterparty web. PwC audit fees are immaterial to SIFI analysis. RISK SIGNAL: The absence of explicit conflict-of-interest policies or recusal procedures for CEO/directors serving on customer/investor boards (Meta, IonQ, Silver Lake portfolio) during compensation setting and audit committee work creates a CIRCULARITY / COST_OPACITY risk where inside information flows and approval chains are opaque."

comp_disc_analysis.notes:
[chunk 1/3] This is a DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis section. SIFI-material signals extracted:

1. AI Revenue Concentration: Broadcom's Semiconductor Solutions Group disclosed 15% of semiconductor revenue from generative AI products in FY2023. While this is a positive revenue driver, it signals growing customer concentration risk in the AI segment as this figure is expected to scale.

2. VMware Execution Risk: The VMware acquisition was so late-closing that its revenue/operating income were excluded from executive incentive plan targets. This underscores integration risk materiality. Combined with a large credit facility drawn for the deal, this represents a significant leverage event.

3. Hidden Leverage / VMware Debt: CFO Spears' individual performance highlights explicitly cite "execution of a credit agreement, which provided funding for the VMware acquisition" — confirming a major debt financing event that will appear on the balance sheet but was flagged here in the comp context.

4. CEO Key-Person / Single-Point-of-Failure: The $160.5M front-loaded PSU for CEO Hock Tan covering FY2023–FY2027 with no annual cash or equity awards during that period is a concentrated key-person dependency. The award is forfeited entirely if AVGO stock never reaches $825 during the earning period (years 3–5), creating a binary compensation structure tied to a single individual's continued tenure and stock price milestones.

5. Peer group named (Accenture, Cisco, Intel, Micron, NVIDIA, Oracle, Salesforce, AMD, Applied Materials, IBM, Lam Research, Mastercard, PayPal, Qualcomm, TI, Visa, ADP) — not extracted as nodes since this is boilerplate benchmarking context with no material relationship disclosure.

No investments in AI labs, SPVs, or circular counterparty relationships were disclosed in this section.
[chunk 2/3] This filing section is Broadcom's DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis (proxy statement). The entire text covers executive compensation tables, PSU/RSU award details, severance benefit agreements, CEO pay ratio, and pay-versus-performance disclosures. There are no SIFI-material entities present: no named business relationships involving customer concentration, supplier dependencies, strategic partnerships, AI lab investments, SPVs, off-balance-sheet entities, capex commitments, revenue round-tripping, or counterparty web disclosures. All content is routine executive compensation boilerplate — share vesting schedules, TSR performance percentiles, severance terms, and pay ratio calculations. Nothing meets the SIFI-materiality threshold defined in the extraction rules. No nodes or edges to emit.
[chunk 3/3] This section of Broadcom's DEF 14A (Compensation Discussion & Analysis, equity plan tables, and stockholder ownership tables) contains no SIFI-material entities. Content is limited to: (1) executive compensation fair-value calculations per ASC 718, (2) equity plan share counts (Avago Plan, 2012 Plan, ESPP, legacy acquired plans from LSI, Brocade, CA Inc.), (3) TSR comparison vs. NASDAQ 100 Index, (4) standard beneficial ownership table showing institutional holders (Vanguard 9.4%, BlackRock 7.5%, Capital World 6.1%, Capital International 5.2%) and director/officer ownership all below 2%. None of these constitute hidden leverage, circularity, revenue roundtripping, capex commitments, off-balance-sheet entities, AI lab investments, customer/supplier concentration, or other SIFI-material signals. No extraction warranted.
